long_biography.plain_text:
Financing industrial buildings on his own account established Thomas R. Whitesell as a major American commercial-property developer. When his New Jersey business struggled to win large contracts, he constructed the facilities itself, using the completed projects to earn bigger assignments and accumulate income-producing property. Master-planned office and warehouse campuses followed throughout the Delaware Valley.

Whitesell also used his Moorestown farm as a community venue, hosting fundraisers and caring for retired racehorses. He served on hospital, education, business and social-service boards, and travelled abroad to help construct hospitals for children awaiting surgery. Away from development, beekeeping and the farm's nature refuge remained enduring personal interests.
